stableMappingPatterns.name: Equity instrument id/description -> Security identifiers
stableMappingPatterns.sourcePattern: instrumentId / instrument description (FpML trade instrument sections)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Equity instruments in the FpML examples are consistently represented as security/observable identifiers in CDM.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Equity product identity is expressed in CDM via security/observable identifier structures; instrument id and description from FpML are used to populate those fields.
caveats: Normalization of identifier namespaces (e.g., exchange codes) occurs in some examples - see exchange-code normalization caveat.
Mapping may combine id + descriptive text to populate multiple CDM identifier fields.

stableMappingPatterns.name: Exchange identifier normalization (FpML exchangeId -> CDM exchange.code)
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: Exchange identifiers present in FpML are mapped to canonical exchange codes in CDM in multiple examples.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Target model uses standardized exchange codes; examples show FpML exchange names/ids translated to a different code space in CDM.
caveats: The precise mapping table or rationale is not present in examples - open questions remain about mapping rules (e.g., 'NASDAQ' -> 'XNAS').
Normalization may be context-dependent (local exchange names vs. global codes).

stableMappingPatterns.name: tradeId -> tradeIdentifier.assignedIdentifier
stableMappingPatterns.explanation: FpML tradeId values are carried into CDM assignedIdentifier entries repeatedly in multiple examples.
stableMappingPatterns.whyItWorksThisWay: Trade-level identifier preservation is required for traceability; examples show a direct mapping from FpML tradeId to CDM assignedIdentifier.
caveats: Some CDM outputs show duplicate tradeIdentifier entries; deduplication rules are not provided and should be verified.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Remove timezone suffix from date strings
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Date/time strings in FpML that include timezone offsets are normalized by removing the timezone suffix when populating CDM date fields.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: FpML unadjusted/adjusted dates with timezone offsets
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.targetSide: CDM date strings without timezone offset
notes: Described explicitly as an important transformation in multiple pair highlights.
Consider canonicalization of date format as a deterministic step prior to CDM population.

repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.name: Dividend and performance terms mapping
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.description: Dividend-related fields and performance payout roles from FpML are translated into CDM dividend/performance payout structures.
repeatedNonLiteralTransformations.sourceSide: FpML dividend terms, payout role references
notes: Mapping occurs in examples but role directionality/party mapping shows inconsistencies in at least one example - treat role mapping carefully.

variantsAndExceptions.name: Duplicate tradeIdentifier entries in CDM
variantsAndExceptions.description: Some CDM outputs contain duplicate tradeIdentifier entries for the same FpML tradeId.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Introduces ambiguity for deduplication logic; consumers should not assume a 1:1 mapping without additional deduplication or identity rules.

variantsAndExceptions.name: PerformancePayout payer/receiver direction mismatch
variantsAndExceptions.description: In at least one example, CDM PerformancePayout payer/receiver roles appear inverted relative to FpML payerPartyReference.
variantsAndExceptions.impactOnGeneralization: Role mapping for payouts may require explicit verification per trade; do not assume party reference semantics are identical between FpML and CDM without confirmation.

suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.name: Party identifiers enriched with generated/default identifiers (e.g., LEI)
suspectedEnrichmentOrDefaultBehavior.description: CDM party identifier elements often include generated or default identifier values that are not present in the source FpML (example: LEI values added).
caution: Treat added identifiers as enrichment rather than source-canonical; do not assume they exist in FpML.
Verify whether enrichment is deterministic for all parties or applied selectively.
